target.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex computer `wait` / `hold_key` outer watchdog deadlines used JavaScript `Number(...)` on free-form `duration` values. Hex strings such as `"0x10"` were accepted (`Number("0x10") === 16`) and silently inflated the deadline, while the downstream computer tool already rejects hex via `readFiniteNumberParam` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Codex contract (sibling `../codex` inspected):** dynamic-tool arguments are `serde_json::Value` with no field-level `duration` guard — `DynamicToolHandler` parses JSON and forwards the value unchanged (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:136`, checkout `bdd282f3bbd55df3a869a5438519cd948c134d4d`). OpenClaw pins `@openai/codex@0.144.4`.

**Canonical downstream grammar (OpenClaw computer tool):**
- Schema: `optionalFiniteNumberSchema` in `src/agents/tools/computer-tool.ts:161`
- Runtime: `readFiniteNumberParam` → `readNumberParam({ strict: true })` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber` (`src/agents/tools/common.ts:228`, `computer-tool.ts:856`)

That parser **rejects hex** (`"0x10"`) and **accepts** decimal / scientific / fractional strings (`"100"`, `"1e2"`, `"100.5"`, `"0.5"`) plus finite numbers.

This PR makes the Codex outer watchdog use the **same** `parseStrictFiniteNumber` path so hex inflation is fixed without underbudgeting fractional/scientific strings that computer-tool still honors.

Collision: overlaps [#107623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107623); this head is the rebased, contract-aligned form.

## User Impact

| Duration input | Before (`Number()`) | After (computer-tool grammar) |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x10"` | +16s inflation | baseline (rejected) |
| `"1e2"` / `"100.5"` / `"0.5"` | coerced | honored (aligned) |
| `0.5` (number) | honored | honored |

## Evidence

Exact head: `d85b72dabe57770b68e901f974a448729cf05581`

### Format and diff check

```
$ git diff --check origin/main..HEAD && echo ok
ok
```

### Vitest suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

Tests cover:
- Hex `"0x10"` — rejected, falls back to baseline (120_000ms)
- Scientific `"1e2"` — honored (250_000ms, 100s duration)
- Fraction `"100.5"` — honored (220_500ms, 100.5s duration)
- Fraction `"0.5"` — honored (120_500ms, 0.5s duration)
- Numeric `0.5` — honored (120_500ms)
- Decimal `"100"` — still honored (220_000ms)

### Real behavior proof — production import vs Number()

The proof script imports `parseStrictFiniteNumber` from the same package (`@openclaw/normalization-core/number-coercion`) used by the production code at `dynamic-tool-execution.ts:524`, and compares it against the old `Number()` behavior on boundary inputs.

```
$ HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) node --import tsx proof-codex-computer-duration-strict.mts
node=v22.22.0
head=d85b72dabe57770b68e901f974a448729cf05581

── Before (Number) vs After (parseStrictFiniteNumber) ──

hex "0x10"               Number: 16       → parseStrict: 0         ← HEX INFLATION FIXED
hex uppercase "0X10"     Number: 16       → parseStrict: 0         ← HEX INFLATION FIXED
decimal "100"            Number: 100      → parseStrict: 100        
scientific "1e2"         Number: 100      → parseStrict: 100        
fraction "100.5"         Number: 100.5    → parseStrict: 100.5      
fraction "0.5"           Number: 0.5      → parseStrict: 0.5        
numeric 100              Number: 100      → parseStrict: 100        
numeric 0.5              Number: 0.5      → parseStrict: 0.5        
negative "-5"            Number: 0        → parseStrict: 0          
garbage "abc"            Number: 0        → parseStrict: 0          
null                     Number: 0        → parseStrict: 0          

Hex inflation fixed: 32 seconds total (both "0x10" and "0X10")

── Behavioral diff: only hex strings change ──
  ok: decimal "100": unchanged (old=100 new=100)
  ok: scientific "1e2": unchanged (old=100 new=100)
  ok: fraction "100.5": unchanged (old=100.5 new=100.5)
  ok: fraction "0.5": unchanged (old=0.5 new=0.5)
  ok: numeric 100: unchanged (old=100 new=100)
  ok: numeric 0.5: unchanged (old=0.5 new=0.5)

── Production-level timeout with hex inflation ──
wait duration="0x10": old=136000ms new=120000ms diff=16000ms (16s)
  ok: Hex "0x10": old inflates by 16s → 136000ms
  ok: Hex "0x10": new baseline → 120000ms
wait duration="100": old=220000ms new=220000ms (identical)
  ok: Normal "100": no regression — old=new=220000ms

── Computer-tool grammar alignment ──
parseStrictFiniteNumber used by both:
  Codex watchdog: readComputerDurationMs (this fix)
  Computer tool:  readFiniteNumberParam (downstream)
  Grammar: rejects hex, accepts decimal/scientific/fraction
  ok: parseStrictFiniteNumber rejects hex "0x10" (undefined)
  ok: parseStrictFiniteNumber accepts decimal "100" (100)
  ok: parseStrictFiniteNumber accepts scientific "1e2" (100)
  ok: parseStrictFiniteNumber accepts fraction "100.5" (100.5)

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 42 passed, 0 failed
```

Key findings:
- **Hex inflation**: `Number("0x10")` = 16 (bug), `parseStrictFiniteNumber("0x10")` = undefined (correct) — saves 16s per hex string
- **Non-hex unchanged**: decimal, scientific, fractional strings produce identical results with both parsers — no regression risk
- **Grammar alignment**: Codex watchdog and computer tool now share the same `parseStrictFiniteNumber` grammar

### Mutation check

Revert `readComputerDurationMs` → `Number()`:
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts -t "aligns computer"

 FAIL  ... > aligns computer duration strings with computer-tool parseStrictFiniteNumber
AssertionError: expected 136000 to be 120000
    at extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts:251:12

 Tests  1 failed | 29 skipped (30)
```
`Number("0x10")` = 16 inflates the deadline to 136000ms instead of the expected 120000ms baseline. Restore → 30/30 passed.

### Codex dependency check

- `../codex/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:127-142` — no field-level `duration` guard, `serde_json::Value` forwarded unchanged
- `@openai/codex@0.144.4` — pinned version
- `readFiniteNumberParam` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber` — same parser used downstream

### Not tested

- Live Codex app-server roundtrip with hex duration arguments (covered by test at the `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` call boundary)
- Non-computer dynamic tool timeout paths (unchanged)
